Spacetime theorem

Repeated physical sites across later windows are valid. The proof indexes fault locations, not distinct output tensor factors. Relative-error factors remain in actual circuit order; overlapping propagated supports and shared spatial Brownian directions do not invalidate the operator-norm tail.

The common fault-span premise is appropriately strong: the same actual continuation must correct arbitrary operator insertions at any allowed set of locations to the same logical isometry, with an input-independent environment factor. Output-site correction alone does not imply this circuit property.

The statistical argument requires a deterministic fixed list of local scripts. Noise- or outcome-dependent selection of later scripts cannot silently be included in the joint Cameron–Martin proof: later relative gates may become discontinuous functions of earlier Gaussian variables.
